## Overview

This notebook picks up the STARmap PLUS control-mouse exploration (Nature Neuroscience 2022, `s41593-022-01251-x`, TauPS2APP dataset, Broad Single Cell Portal SCP1375) and does two things:

1. **Reproduces the spatial check in R** -- the same cell-type-colored spatial scatter plot already built and validated in Python for the 4 control samples (`8months`/`13months` x `replicate_1`/`replicate_2`), using the identical categorical palette, so the two are visually interchangeable.
2. **Builds a Seurat object** for those same 4 control samples, joining raw counts (`expression_matrix_raw.csv`), cell metadata (`metadata.csv`), and per-cell spatial coordinates (`spatial_*-control-replicate_*.csv`) into one object usable for downstream work (e.g. a mistyR-style spatial-proximity analysis).

**Important -- read before running Part 2.** `expression_matrix_raw.csv` is ~800MB and has not been inspected at all yet: its orientation (genes as rows or columns) and its cell-identifier scheme are both unknown. `NAME` in the metadata/spatial files is confirmed unique only *within* a given `label` (sample), not globally -- so cells must be matched using the composite key `(label, NAME)`, not `NAME` alone. Part 2 is therefore written diagnostic-first: it peeks at the file cheaply (header only, then a handful of rows) and prints what it finds, *before* committing to any assumption about structure. Run it chunk-by-chunk, look at the printed output, and only flip `run_full_load` to `TRUE` once the diagnostics make sense -- this mirrors how the STRINGdb background-column and duplicate-factor-level issues earlier in this project were resolved: diagnose first, then act, rather than guessing.

```{r setup}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(Matrix)
library(Seurat)

data_dir <- "STARmap_PLUS_data"

# Same out_dir + dir.create() + file.path() convention 01/02/03 use for their saved
# objects, so this notebook's outputs land in their own folder rather than flat
# alongside the .qmd.
out_dir <- "starmap_plus_processed"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Part 1 -- Spatial plot (R translation)

### Load the 4 control coordinate files

Each file's second row is the Broad Single Cell Portal's `TYPE` metadata row, not data, and gets skipped the same way the Python version did (`skiprows=[1]`).

```{r load-spatial}
#| label: load-spatial

spatial_files <- c(
  "8months-control-replicate_1"  = file.path(data_dir, "spatial_8months-control-replicate_1.csv"),
  "8months-control-replicate_2"  = file.path(data_dir, "spatial_8months-control-replicate_2.csv"),
  "13months-control-replicate_1" = file.path(data_dir, "spatial_13months-control-replicate_1.csv"),
  "13months-control-replicate_2" = file.path(data_dir, "spatial_13months-control-replicate_2.csv")
)

panel_order <- names(spatial_files)

read_scp_cluster_file <- function(path) {
  # Line 1 is the real header, line 2 is SCP's "TYPE" row (e.g. "TYPE,numeric,numeric,...").
  # Both lines have to be skipped manually (skip = 2), not just the TYPE row, or the TYPE
  # row's text values ("numeric") get read as data and coerce X/Y to character.
  #
  # header = FALSE is essential here and was missing in an earlier version of this
  # function: read.csv() defaults to header = TRUE regardless of whether col.names is
  # also supplied, so without it, the first genuine DATA row (right after skip = 2) was
  # being consumed as a header line and silently discarded -- exactly one real cell lost
  # per file, which is what caused coords_for_seurat to come up 4 cells short overall
  # (one missing from each of the 4 samples) in Part 4.
  #
  # colClasses forces X/Y to numeric regardless of what read.csv's own type-guessing
  # would otherwise have done.
  out <- read.csv(path, skip = 2, header = FALSE,
                   col.names = c("NAME", "X", "Y", "X_scaled", "Y_scaled",
                                 "label", "top_level_cell_type", "sub_level_cell_type"),
                   colClasses = c("character", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric", "numeric",
                                  "character", "character", "character"))
  stopifnot(is.numeric(out$X), is.numeric(out$Y))  # fail loudly here, not deep inside a plot call
  out
}

spatial_all <- map_dfr(spatial_files, read_scp_cluster_file) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = panel_order))

spatial_all
```

### Cell-type palette (identical to the Python check)

Fixed hex assignment per `top_level_cell_type`, carried over unchanged from the validated Python plot so both are directly comparable.

```{r palette}
#| label: palette

cell_type_palette <- c(
  "Astro"  = "#1f77b4",
  "CA1"    = "#ff7f0e",
  "CA2"    = "#2ca02c",
  "CA3"    = "#d62728",
  "CTX-Ex" = "#9467bd",
  "DG"     = "#8c564b",
  "Endo"   = "#e377c2",
  "Inh"    = "#7f7f7f",
  "LHb"    = "#bcbd22",
  "Micro"  = "#17becf",
  "OPC"    = "#aec7e8",
  "Oligo"  = "#ffbb78",
  "SMC"    = "#98df8a"
)

spatial_all <- spatial_all |>
  mutate(top_level_cell_type = factor(top_level_cell_type, levels = names(cell_type_palette)))
```

### Plot

2x2 grid, one panel per sample, image-style coordinates (`y` flipped, as in the Python `invert_yaxis()` call) and equal aspect so anatomy isn't distorted.

Each sample has its own X/Y coordinate range, so each panel needs an *independently* auto-scaled, equal-aspect axis -- exactly what the Python version got for free from separate matplotlib subplots (`ax.set_aspect('equal')` called per-panel). `ggplot2`'s own `facet_wrap()` can't do that: as of ggplot2 3.5, `facet_wrap(scales = "free")` is not allowed together with `coord_fixed()` (a fixed-ratio `coord_cartesian()`) -- it errors in `draw_panels()`. So instead of one faceted plot, this builds 4 separate `coord_fixed()` plots (one per sample) and combines them with `patchwork`, which reproduces the "independent subplots" layout the Python matplotlib version actually used.

```{r spatial-plot}
#| label: spatial-plot
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10

# Named lookup label -> "label (n=... cells)", used as each panel's title.
panel_titles <- spatial_all |>
  count(label, name = "n_cells", .drop = FALSE) |>
  mutate(panel_title = sprintf("%s  (n=%s cells)", label, format(n_cells, big.mark = ","))) |>
  select(label, panel_title) |>
  deframe()

plot_one_sample <- function(lbl) {
  sub <- spatial_all |> filter(label == lbl)
  ggplot(sub, aes(x = X, y = Y, color = top_level_cell_type)) +
    geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.9, stroke = 0) +
    scale_color_manual(values = cell_type_palette, name = "Cell type", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_y_reverse() +
    coord_fixed() +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
    labs(title = panel_titles[[as.character(lbl)]]) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"))
}

panel_plots <- map(panel_order, plot_one_sample)

wrap_plots(panel_plots, ncol = 2) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "STARmap PLUS -- control mice, spatial coordinates by cell type",
    theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14))
  )
# (legend.position is left at ggplot2's default of "right" here -- the patchwork "&"
# operator that would normally apply a theme tweak to every sub-plot is skipped
# because Seurat's S4/Bioconductor-style dependencies can redefine `&` as an S4
# generic in the same session, which shadows patchwork's own S3 method for it.)
```

## Part 2 -- Diagnose `expression_matrix_raw.csv` before loading it

Do not try to load this file in full until the checks below make sense. It's read here only in cheap slices via `read.csv(..., nrows = ...)`, never the whole ~800MB at once.

```{r inspect-matrix-raw-lines}
#| label: inspect-matrix-raw-lines

matrix_path <- file.path(data_dir, "expression_matrix_raw.csv")

# Ground truth, plain-text, no parsing library involved at all.
raw_lines <- readLines(matrix_path, n = 2)
cat("Line 1, first 300 characters:\n")
cat(substr(raw_lines[1], 1, 300), "\n\n")
cat("Line 2, first 300 characters:\n")
cat(substr(raw_lines[2], 1, 300), "\n")
```

Line 1 turned out to be `GENE,1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,13,14,15,...` -- a real header, with the file's first column literally named `GENE` (confirming genes as rows) and every other column named by a bare integer. Those integers skip around (2 and 12 are both missing from that run) rather than counting `1,2,3,4,...` continuously, which is the signature of an *original* numbering that had some cells dropped by QC -- exactly what `metadata.csv`'s `orig_index` column is for. That's a strong hypothesis, not a confirmed fact yet, so `inspect-matrix-id-match` below tests it directly against the real metadata rather than assuming it.

(A `data.table::fread(..., nrows = 0)` read of this same file earlier reported column names `V1, V2, ...` instead of `GENE, 1, 3, 4, ...` -- that was `fread`'s own header auto-detection guessing wrong, not a sign the header doesn't exist. Column headers that are themselves bare integers look enough like the numeric data below them to fool a heuristic that decides "header vs. no header" by comparing the type profile of row 1 against subsequent rows. `read.csv()` below is told `header = TRUE` explicitly rather than relying on any such guess.)

```{r inspect-matrix-peek}
#| label: inspect-matrix-peek

# nrows keeps this cheap despite the ~800MB file -- read.csv's nrows argument stops
# after that many data lines rather than reading the whole file first.
# check.names = FALSE is essential: the integer column names ("1","3","4",...) would
# otherwise get silently mangled into syntactic names ("X1","X3","X4") by read.csv's
# default check.names = TRUE.
matrix_peek <- read.csv(matrix_path, header = TRUE, nrows = 5, check.names = FALSE)
n_cols <- ncol(matrix_peek)

cat("Number of columns:", n_cols, "\n")
cat("First column name (gene-ID column):", names(matrix_peek)[1], "\n")
cat("First 10 cell-ID column names:\n")
print(head(names(matrix_peek)[-1], 10))
cat("\nFirst 5 gene names (first data column, first 5 rows):\n")
print(matrix_peek[[1]])
```

```{r inspect-matrix-id-match}
#| label: inspect-matrix-id-match

# Full metadata.csv, read once here and reused in Part 3/4. Not subset to a few
# columns (unlike the previous fread-based version) since read.csv doesn't have an
# equivalent cheap column-select, and the whole file is small (~18MB) regardless.
#
# metadata.csv turns out to follow the same Broad SCP convention as the spatial
# cluster files (Part 1): row 1 after the header is the "TYPE" metadata row
# (NAME == "TYPE", every other field == "group"), not real data. read.csv has no
# manual col.names supplied here (unlike read_scp_cluster_file), so it DOES use line 1
# as the header correctly -- the problem is only that the TYPE row then gets read in
# as data row 1, which is why NAME/orig_index came back as character instead of
# integer (that stray "TYPE"/"group" text forces the whole column to character).
metadata_all <- read.csv(file.path(data_dir, "metadata.csv"))
metadata_all <- metadata_all[metadata_all$NAME != "TYPE", ]
metadata_all$NAME <- as.integer(metadata_all$NAME)
metadata_all$orig_index <- as.integer(metadata_all$orig_index)

n_cells_total   <- nrow(metadata_all)
n_cells_control <- metadata_all |> filter(label %in% panel_order) |> nrow()
cat("Total cells in metadata.csv:", n_cells_total, "\n")
cat("Cells in the 4 control samples:", n_cells_control, "(expected 35,771)\n\n")

# Test the id-matching hypotheses against the matrix's actual column names (from the
# cheap peek above -- the column *names* are identical whether we read 5 rows or all
# of them, so this doesn't require the full read).
matrix_col_ids <- names(matrix_peek)[-1]

name_hits     <- sum(matrix_col_ids %in% as.character(metadata_all$NAME))
composite_ids <- paste0(metadata_all$label, "_", metadata_all$NAME)
composite_hits <- sum(matrix_col_ids %in% composite_ids)
origidx_hits  <- sum(matrix_col_ids %in% as.character(metadata_all$orig_index))

cat("Of", length(matrix_col_ids), "column IDs in the matrix header:\n")
cat(" - matched metadata$NAME directly:", name_hits, "\n")
cat(" - matched metadata's label_NAME composite:", composite_hits, "\n")
cat(" - matched metadata$orig_index:", origidx_hits, "\n")
cat("\nWhichever count is highest (ideally close to", length(matrix_col_ids), ") is the field to key on below.\n")
```

**Important correction.** `orig_index` looked like a promising global key from the id-match counts above, but building the count matrix by *matching on that text* (`intersect(names(expr_df), control_meta$cell_id)`, an earlier version of `build-count-matrix`) silently produced a matrix with only 9,428 cells instead of the expected 35,771. The cause: `orig_index` is not actually unique across samples -- it looks like a per-section index that resets for each biosample, so the same digits ("1", "3", "4", ...) recur once per sample. `expression_matrix_raw.csv` was read with `check.names = FALSE` specifically to preserve those integer column names as-is, which means duplicate column names really do exist side-by-side in `expr_df` once the full file is read. Selecting columns *by name* (`df[, "5"]`) against duplicated names silently returns only the first match, so most of the 4 samples' cells got dropped in favor of whichever sample's block of indices happened to be matched first -- landing, by chance, on a count equal to one single sample's size.

The fix is to stop matching by name entirely and instead match by **row/column position**, which is unambiguous regardless of what text label sits on top of each column. This only works if the matrix's columns are in the same order as `metadata.csv`'s rows -- the diagnostic below checks that directly before Part 3 relies on it.

```{r inspect-matrix-position-check}
#| label: inspect-matrix-position-check

# names(matrix_peek) already reflects the FULL column set (header parsing doesn't
# depend on how many data rows -- nrows -- were read), so this needs no further reads.
matrix_ids_all <- names(matrix_peek)[-1]

same_length <- length(matrix_ids_all) == nrow(metadata_all)
same_order  <- if (same_length) identical(matrix_ids_all, as.character(metadata_all$orig_index)) else FALSE

cat("Data columns in expression_matrix_raw.csv:", length(matrix_ids_all), "\n")
cat("Rows in metadata.csv:", nrow(metadata_all), "\n")
cat("Same length:", same_length, "\n")
cat("Column order matches metadata_all$orig_index row-for-row:", same_order, "\n")

if (same_order) {
  cat("\n-> Confirmed: matrix column i corresponds to metadata_all row i. Part 3 below",
      "selects columns by that row position, not by the (non-unique) orig_index text.\n")
} else {
  cat("\n-> NOT confirmed -- do not flip run_full_load yet. Compare a slice of",
      "matrix_ids_all against metadata_all$orig_index by eye (e.g. print both side by",
      "side for the first ~30 entries) to see where the correspondence breaks.\n")
}
```

**Stop here and read the printed output before continuing.** `build-count-matrix` below only runs the position-based approach once `run_full_load` is flipped to `TRUE` -- do that only after `same_order` above prints `TRUE`.

## Part 3 -- Build the control-subset count matrix

```{r build-count-matrix}
#| label: build-count-matrix

run_full_load <- FALSE  # set to TRUE once inspect-matrix-position-check prints same_order = TRUE

if (run_full_load) {

  # Which metadata_all rows are the 4 control samples, in their existing row order --
  # this same integer vector indexes BOTH metadata_all's rows and expr_df's columns
  # (offset by +1 for the leading GENE column), which is what keeps the two aligned
  # without any name-based matching.
  control_row_positions <- which(metadata_all$label %in% panel_order)

  # Fresh sequential "Cell_<n>" names, NOT "Cell_<orig_index>" -- orig_index (and NAME)
  # are confirmed non-unique across the 4 samples (that's what caused the 9,428-cell
  # bug), so prefixing "Cell_" onto them could still collide. A plain 1..35771 sequence
  # in the same row order as control_row_positions is guaranteed unique; the original
  # orig_index/NAME/label fields are kept as ordinary metadata columns for traceability.
  #
  # tibble::remove_rownames() matters here: metadata_all[control_row_positions, ] is
  # base-R subsetting, which keeps metadata_all's ORIGINAL row names (e.g. "5", "6",
  # "8", ...) attached rather than renumbering them -- and column_to_rownames() in
  # Part 4 refuses to run on a data frame that already carries non-default row names.
  control_meta <- metadata_all[control_row_positions, ] |>
    tibble::remove_rownames() |>
    mutate(cell_id = paste0("Cell_", dplyr::row_number()))

  stopifnot(nrow(control_meta) == 35771)          # sanity check against the known control cell count
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(control_meta$cell_id))  # must be unique by construction -- fail loudly if not

  # Full read -- genes x cells, first column = gene symbol. read.csv (not fread), per
  # preference, even though it's slower/heavier on memory for an ~800MB file.
  expr_df <- read.csv(matrix_path, header = TRUE, check.names = FALSE)
  gene_names <- expr_df[[1]]

  # Select by POSITION (control_row_positions + 1, to skip the GENE column), not by
  # name -- see the "Important correction" note above Part 2's position-check diagnostic
  # for why name-based selection silently lost most of the 35,771 cells.
  expr_mat <- as.matrix(expr_df[, control_row_positions + 1])
  rownames(expr_mat) <- gene_names
  colnames(expr_mat) <- control_meta$cell_id

  counts_sparse <- Matrix::Matrix(expr_mat, sparse = TRUE)
  rm(expr_df, expr_mat); gc()

  saveRDS(counts_sparse, file.path(out_dir, "starmap_plus_control_counts.rds"))

  cat("Built control-subset count matrix:", nrow(counts_sparse), "genes x", ncol(counts_sparse), "cells\n")

} else {
  cat("run_full_load is FALSE -- skipping the ~800MB read. Confirm the diagnostics above first.\n")
}
```

## Part 4 -- Assemble the Seurat object

Only runs once Part 3 has produced `counts_sparse`. Coordinates are attached as a custom `spatial` `DimReduc` (the STARmap PLUS data isn't a Visium slide, so there's no `images` slot to populate -- a 2-D reduction is the simplest way to keep per-cell X/Y attached to the object and plottable with `Seurat::DimPlot(obj, reduction = "spatial")`).

```{r build-seurat}
#| label: build-seurat

if (run_full_load && exists("counts_sparse")) {

  # control_meta's row order and counts_sparse's column order are already identical --
  # both were built from the same control_row_positions vector in Part 3 -- so this is
  # a direct rowname assignment, not a re-match/re-order.
  meta_for_seurat <- control_meta |>
    column_to_rownames("cell_id")

  starmap_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(
    counts    = counts_sparse,
    meta.data = meta_for_seurat,
    project   = "STARmapPLUS_control"
  )

  # Attach spatial coordinates (X, Y) from the per-sample coordinate files. Those files
  # only carry NAME (not our new cell_id), so bridge through control_meta -- matched on
  # the composite (label, NAME) key, which IS unique -- to recover each cell's cell_id
  # before joining onto the counts matrix's column names. The join key is built as a
  # plain pasted string on both sides (not a typed dplyr join on label/NAME directly) to
  # sidestep factor-vs-character / integer-vs-character type mismatches between the two
  # tables' columns.
  name_to_cell_id <- control_meta |>
    transmute(join_key = paste(as.character(label), NAME, sep = "___"), cell_id)

  coords_for_seurat <- spatial_all |>
    mutate(join_key = paste(as.character(label), NAME, sep = "___")) |>
    left_join(name_to_cell_id, by = "join_key") |>
    filter(!is.na(cell_id), cell_id %in% colnames(starmap_obj)) |>
    distinct(cell_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    arrange(match(cell_id, colnames(starmap_obj))) |>
    select(cell_id, X, Y)

  # Diagnostics BEFORE the stopifnot, so a mismatch prints exactly what's missing
  # instead of just halting -- same "show the evidence, don't just fail" approach
  # used throughout this notebook.
  cat("coords_for_seurat rows:", nrow(coords_for_seurat), " | ncol(starmap_obj):", ncol(starmap_obj), "\n")

  # Per-sample counts on both sides -- a mismatch confined to one sample points at
  # that sample's label text or NAME values specifically, not a global join problem.
  cat("\ncontrol_meta rows per label:\n")
  print(table(control_meta$label))
  cat("\nspatial_all rows per label:\n")
  print(table(spatial_all$label))

  missing_cell_ids <- setdiff(colnames(starmap_obj), coords_for_seurat$cell_id)
  cat("\nCells in starmap_obj with NO matched spatial coordinate:", length(missing_cell_ids), "\n")
  if (length(missing_cell_ids) > 0) {
    missing_preview <- control_meta[control_meta$cell_id %in% head(missing_cell_ids, 10),
                                     c("cell_id", "label", "NAME")]
    cat("A sample of unmatched cells (check these NAME/label values against spatial_all by eye):\n")
    print(missing_preview)
  }

  stopifnot(nrow(coords_for_seurat) == ncol(starmap_obj))

  spatial_emb <- as.matrix(coords_for_seurat |> select(X, Y))
  rownames(spatial_emb) <- coords_for_seurat$cell_id
  colnames(spatial_emb) <- c("spatial_1", "spatial_2")

  starmap_obj[["spatial"]] <- CreateDimReducObject(
    embeddings = spatial_emb,
    key = "spatial_",
    assay = DefaultAssay(starmap_obj)
  )

  saveRDS(starmap_obj, file.path(out_dir, "starmap_plus_control_seurat.rds"))

  starmap_obj

} else {
  cat("Seurat object not built yet -- run Part 3 (run_full_load <- TRUE) first.\n")
}
```

## Part 5 -- Verify: reproduce the spatial plot from `starmap_obj` itself

Sanity check, independent of Part 1's plot: pull coordinates and cell types back out of the finished Seurat object -- not from `spatial_all`/`control_meta` directly -- and redraw the same 4-panel plot. If `starmap_obj` was assembled correctly (counts, metadata, and the `spatial` reduction all genuinely aligned to the same 35,771 cells), this should look identical to Part 1's plot. Any visible difference -- a shuffled cell-type pattern, a shifted/mirrored tissue outline, a panel with the wrong sample's shape -- would mean something is still misaligned somewhere in Part 3/4, despite the `stopifnot()` checks passing.

```{r verify-seurat-plot}
#| label: verify-seurat-plot
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10

if (exists("starmap_obj")) {

  verify_coords <- as.data.frame(Embeddings(starmap_obj, "spatial"))
  verify_coords$cell_id <- rownames(verify_coords)

  verify_meta <- starmap_obj@meta.data
  verify_meta$cell_id <- rownames(verify_meta)

  verify_df <- verify_coords |>
    left_join(verify_meta |> select(cell_id, label, top_level_cell_type), by = "cell_id") |>
    mutate(
      label = factor(label, levels = panel_order),
      top_level_cell_type = factor(top_level_cell_type, levels = names(cell_type_palette))
    )

  stopifnot(nrow(verify_df) == ncol(starmap_obj))  # every cell got a coordinate + cell type back

  verify_panel_titles <- verify_df |>
    count(label, name = "n_cells", .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(panel_title = sprintf("%s  (n=%s cells)", label, format(n_cells, big.mark = ","))) |>
    select(label, panel_title) |>
    deframe()

  plot_one_sample_verify <- function(lbl) {
    sub <- verify_df |> filter(label == lbl)
    ggplot(sub, aes(x = spatial_1, y = spatial_2, color = top_level_cell_type)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.9, stroke = 0) +
      scale_color_manual(values = cell_type_palette, name = "Cell type", drop = FALSE) +
      scale_y_reverse() +
      coord_fixed() +
      guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
      labs(title = verify_panel_titles[[as.character(lbl)]]) +
      theme_void(base_size = 12) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"))
  }

  verify_plots <- map(panel_order, plot_one_sample_verify)

  wrap_plots(verify_plots, ncol = 2) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Verification -- same plot, rebuilt entirely from starmap_obj",
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14))
    )

} else {
  cat("starmap_obj doesn't exist yet -- run Part 3 and Part 4 (run_full_load <- TRUE) first.\n")
}
```

## Part 6 -- Restrict to hippocampus only

`metadata.csv`'s `region` field (`Alveus`, `Hippocampus`, `Cortex`, `Corpus Callosum`) already carries the anatomical annotation needed for this -- no coordinate-based cropping required. First, a look at how the regions break down before touching anything:

```{r region-breakdown}
#| label: region-breakdown

if (exists("starmap_obj")) {
  cat("Cells per region (all 4 samples combined):\n")
  print(table(starmap_obj$region))
  cat("\nCells per region_merged:\n")
  print(table(starmap_obj$region_merged))
  cat("\nCells per region x sample:\n")
  print(table(starmap_obj$region, starmap_obj$label))
} else {
  cat("starmap_obj doesn't exist yet -- run Part 3 and Part 4 first.\n")
}
```

Then the actual subset. `starmap_obj` (all regions) is kept as-is and saved separately from this hippocampus-only version -- non-destructive, so the full object is still there for reference/QC (e.g. re-running `verify-seurat-plot`-style checks) even once `starmap_hpc` becomes the one used downstream.

```{r subset-hippocampus}
#| label: subset-hippocampus

if (exists("starmap_obj")) {
  starmap_hpc <- subset(starmap_obj, subset = region == "Hippocampus")

  cat("Hippocampus-only:", ncol(starmap_hpc), "cells (from", ncol(starmap_obj), "total)\n")
  cat("\nPer-sample counts, hippocampus only:\n")
  print(table(starmap_hpc$label))

  saveRDS(starmap_hpc, file.path(out_dir, "starmap_plus_control_seurat_hippocampus.rds"))
} else {
  cat("starmap_obj doesn't exist yet -- run Part 3 and Part 4 first.\n")
}
```

Same plot style as Part 5, rebuilt on `starmap_hpc` -- each panel's axes will zoom in automatically to just the hippocampal footprint, since `coord_fixed()` scales to whatever data is actually present in each sample.

```{r hippocampus-plot}
#| label: hippocampus-plot
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10

if (exists("starmap_hpc")) {

  hpc_coords <- as.data.frame(Embeddings(starmap_hpc, "spatial"))
  hpc_coords$cell_id <- rownames(hpc_coords)

  hpc_meta <- starmap_hpc@meta.data
  hpc_meta$cell_id <- rownames(hpc_meta)

  hpc_df <- hpc_coords |>
    left_join(hpc_meta |> select(cell_id, label, top_level_cell_type), by = "cell_id") |>
    mutate(
      label = factor(label, levels = panel_order),
      top_level_cell_type = factor(top_level_cell_type, levels = names(cell_type_palette))
    )

  hpc_panel_titles <- hpc_df |>
    count(label, name = "n_cells", .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(panel_title = sprintf("%s  (n=%s cells)", label, format(n_cells, big.mark = ","))) |>
    select(label, panel_title) |>
    deframe()

  plot_one_sample_hpc <- function(lbl) {
    sub <- hpc_df |> filter(label == lbl)
    ggplot(sub, aes(x = spatial_1, y = spatial_2, color = top_level_cell_type)) +
      geom_point(size = 1.1, alpha = 0.9, stroke = 0) +
      scale_color_manual(values = cell_type_palette, name = "Cell type", drop = FALSE) +
      scale_y_reverse() +
      coord_fixed() +
      guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
      labs(title = hpc_panel_titles[[as.character(lbl)]]) +
      theme_void(base_size = 12) +
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"))
  }

  hpc_plots <- map(panel_order, plot_one_sample_hpc)

  wrap_plots(hpc_plots, ncol = 2) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "STARmap PLUS -- hippocampus only, control mice",
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14))
    )

} else {
  cat("starmap_hpc doesn't exist yet -- run subset-hippocampus above first.\n")
}
```

## Part 7 -- Highlight one or more cell types

Same 4-panel layout, but everything except the chosen `top_level_cell_type`(s) is drawn in flat grey first, then those types are drawn on top in their real palette colors -- the standard way to make specific populations stand out against tissue context without losing the rest as a spatial reference. `highlight_types` takes a vector, so highlighting one type or several works the same way. Rebuilt directly from `starmap_hpc` (the hippocampus-only object), independent of any earlier chunk's variables, so it can be re-run on its own.

```{r highlight-celltype}
#| label: highlight-celltype
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10

highlight_types <- c("Micro", "OPC", "Astro", "Endo")  # any subset of names(cell_type_palette) -- one or several

if (exists("starmap_hpc")) {

  stopifnot(all(highlight_types %in% names(cell_type_palette)))

  hl_coords <- as.data.frame(Embeddings(starmap_hpc, "spatial"))
  hl_coords$cell_id <- rownames(hl_coords)

  hl_meta <- starmap_hpc@meta.data
  hl_meta$cell_id <- rownames(hl_meta)

  hl_df <- hl_coords |>
    left_join(hl_meta |> select(cell_id, label, top_level_cell_type), by = "cell_id") |>
    mutate(label = factor(label, levels = panel_order))

  hl_panel_titles <- hl_df |>
    count(label, name = "n_cells", .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(panel_title = sprintf("%s  (n=%s cells)", label, format(n_cells, big.mark = ","))) |>
    select(label, panel_title) |>
    deframe()

  plot_one_sample_highlight <- function(lbl) {
    sub        <- hl_df |> filter(label == lbl)
    background <- sub |> filter(!top_level_cell_type %in% highlight_types)
    foreground <- sub |>
      filter(top_level_cell_type %in% highlight_types) |>
      mutate(top_level_cell_type = factor(top_level_cell_type, levels = highlight_types))

    per_type_n <- foreground |> count(top_level_cell_type, name = "n", .drop = FALSE)
    subtitle_txt <- paste(sprintf("%s: n=%s", per_type_n$top_level_cell_type, format(per_type_n$n, big.mark = ",")),
                           collapse = "   ")

    ggplot() +
      geom_point(data = background, aes(x = spatial_1, y = spatial_2),
                 color = "grey85", size = 1.1, alpha = 0.6, stroke = 0) +
      geom_point(data = foreground, aes(x = spatial_1, y = spatial_2, color = top_level_cell_type),
                 size = 1.3, alpha = 0.95, stroke = 0) +
      scale_color_manual(values = cell_type_palette[highlight_types], name = "Cell type", drop = FALSE) +
      scale_y_reverse() +
      coord_fixed() +
      guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
      labs(title = hl_panel_titles[[as.character(lbl)]], subtitle = subtitle_txt) +
      theme_void(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8)
      )
  }

  highlight_plots <- map(panel_order, plot_one_sample_highlight)

  wrap_plots(highlight_plots, ncol = 2) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
      title = paste("STARmap PLUS, hippocampus only -- highlighting", paste(highlight_types, collapse = ", ")),
      theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14))
    )

} else {
  cat("starmap_hpc doesn't exist yet -- run subset-hippocampus (Part 6) first.\n")
}
```

To highlight against the full (all-regions) object instead, swap `starmap_hpc` for `starmap_obj` in the two `Embeddings()`/`@meta.data` lines above -- everything else works unchanged, since it doesn't depend on `hpc_df` or any other earlier chunk's state.

## Notes on interpretation

`expression_matrix_raw.csv`'s exact layout was not known ahead of writing this notebook, so Part 2 exists to find out empirically rather than guessing -- the same "diagnose first" approach this project has used for the STRINGdb background-column detection and the duplicate-factor-level bug earlier on. The first working version of Part 3 matched cells by *name* (their `orig_index` text) and that produced a silently wrong result -- 9,428 cells instead of 35,771 -- because `orig_index` turned out not to be globally unique (it resets per sample), so name-based column selection quietly kept only the first match for each repeated digit string. The current version matches by row/column *position* instead, which is unambiguous regardless of what text sits on each column, gated behind `inspect-matrix-position-check` confirming that the matrix's column order really does correspond to `metadata.csv`'s row order.

Cell identifiers in the final object are fresh sequential `Cell_1`, `Cell_2`, ... names rather than `Cell_<orig_index>` or `Cell_<NAME>`, for the same reason: those original fields aren't unique across the 4 samples, so prefixing them would just relocate the collision risk into the final object instead of removing it. The original `orig_index`, `NAME`, and `label` values are all still present as ordinary metadata columns on `starmap_obj` if you need to trace a `Cell_n` back to its source row.

Once the object builds successfully, `starmap_obj$region`, `starmap_obj$top_level_cell_type`, and `starmap_obj$time` (8 vs 13 months) are the columns most relevant to the aging comparison discussed earlier -- e.g. as grouping variables for a future mistyR run using `starmap_obj@reductions$spatial` for the juxtaview/paraview neighborhood construction.

`starmap_hpc` (Part 6) is the hippocampus-restricted object intended for that downstream analysis -- filtered on `region == "Hippocampus"` alone, not `Alveus` (the adjacent white-matter tract), so it's gray-matter-only. If a mistyR-style analysis ends up wanting the immediately bordering white matter too (e.g. because axonal input/output through the alveus matters for a specific question), that's a one-line change to the `subset()` filter in `subset-hippocampus` (`region %in% c("Hippocampus", "Alveus")`). Both `starmap_obj` (all regions) and `starmap_hpc` (hippocampus only) are saved to separate `.rds` files, so neither has to be rebuilt from scratch to get the other back.
